note: Hand checks of test names where our list (Wikidata/GLEIF) looks out of date or the answer is ambiguous. accept = countries counted as right (rule: the country the ultimate owner is run from; private equity = the firm's head office; franchise = brand owner). skip = left out of the score because the right answer is unclear or the name is ambiguous. Sources are news reports or Wikipedia pages read on the day.

ASDA.why: Walmart sold Asda in 2021; TDR Capital (London) is now the majority owner.

MORRISONS DAILY.why: Morrisons has been owned by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (New York private equity) since 2021.

WELCOME BREAK.why: Welcome Break is majority-owned by Applegreen, which has been majority-owned by Blackstone since 2021.

SHARPS.why: Sharps Bedrooms is owned by Epiris, a London private-equity firm (not Sun Capital).

EVANS.why: City Chic sold Evans in 2023 to AK Retail Holdings (owner of Yours Clothing and M&Co, Peterborough).

FIRED EARTH.why: The Fired Earth name was bought by Topps Tiles; no longer part of Middleby.

PREZZO.why: Bought in 2023 by Cain International, an investor run from London and Los Angeles.

FARMHOUSE INNS.why: A Greene King brand; Greene King is owned by CK Asset Holdings, run from Hong Kong (our list said CN because of how Wikidata records Hong Kong).

TEMU.why: PDD Holdings' head office has been in Dublin since 2023, but the business is largely run from China; both are defensible.

ESSAR ENERGY.why: Essar is controlled by the Ruia family, who run it from Mumbai and London.

BETTER.why: Ambiguous: GLL's 'Better' leisure centres (GB) or Better.com (US).

MACE.why: Ambiguous: the Mace convenience symbol group (different owners in GB and Northern Ireland) or Mace the construction company.

MACE NORTHERN IRELAND.why: Current owner of the Mace NI franchise not confirmed.

FITNESS FIRST.why: The UK clubs passed to DW Sports in 2016 and DW to Frasers Group in 2020; current owner of the UK Fitness First clubs not confirmed.

A&O HOSTELS.why: Current owner not confirmed (founder-run, previously TPG Real Estate; our list says StepStone).

OVO.why: E.ON completed its takeover of OVO Energy on 8 October 2026.

FABB FURNITURE.why: Bought by Nick Scali (Australia, listed) to enter the UK.

OBRIENS CAFE.why: BWG Group bought O'Briens in June 2026; BWG is wholly owned by SPAR South Africa.

EASYJET.why: Apollo's takeover was agreed in August 2026 but completes next year; until then easyJet plc is its own owner.

BOOTS.why: Sycamore Partners (US) owns Boots; its sale to Wittington Investments and Fairfax (Canada), agreed on 7 October 2026, hasn't completed.

PRET A MANGER.why: Owned by JAB Holding (run from Luxembourg), which is controlled by Germany's Reimann family; both are defensible.

PETIT PRET.why: Part of Pret A Manger; see PRET A MANGER.

PARKERS.why: Ambiguous: Parkers estate agents (GB) or the Parkers car-price guide (Bauer Media, DE).
